slice.name: repository-transport stale-CAS conflict fail-closed probe
slice.tested_scope: Attempt an update of the current immutable role-local predecessor artifact through the exposed GitHub update-file surface while intentionally supplying a stale predecessor blob SHA instead of the current target blob SHA. Use byte-equivalent content so the only tested boundary is optimistic-concurrency authority. Then exact-read the target path and verify its blob is unchanged. This scope tests stale-CAS conflict rejection on GitHub Contents transport only; it does not establish idempotency of arbitrary non-repository production effects.

assessment.claim: For the exact GitHub Contents stale-update scope, the exposed Chat repository update path rejected a stale blob authority with HTTP 409 and the target artifact remained on the same blob after readback.
limitations: The observed 409 is a repository optimistic-concurrency guard, not proof that external production actions are conflict-safe or idempotent.
No non-repository production-effect surface was exercised because none was selected within this role-local zero-cost, zero-finite-quota, non-user-side-effect slice.
No authentic rate-limit recovery or real account quota exhaustion was observed.
This slice is not Phase-1 acceptance or completion evidence by itself.

continuation.next_action: On the next reproducibility_auditor invocation, reconstruct current downstream authority and test exactly one still-unproven boundary without repeating transport creation/readback, fail-open configuration, denial replay, synthetic 429, optional-monthly-quota-zero replay, duplicate-create, or stale-CAS conflict probes. Prefer a safely authorized directly exposed non-repository production-effect surface with an idempotency key or duplicate replay; otherwise capture an authentic naturally occurring rate-limit/resume, account-quota exhaustion, richer-mode computation parity boundary, or a distinct role-local missing-tool boundary. Keep production-effect idempotency, authentic rate-limit recovery, authentic account-quota exhaustion, richer-mode computation parity, and global Phase-1 acceptance unresolved unless directly evidenced.
